messages:
emma (eng-platform): quick flag 1: we just got a small customer complaint + a billing spike. Root cause looks like strict validator rejecting toolhook responses that are shape-variants (array vs object). Many of those fell back to degen and got billed there.

priya (observability): I see the spike on the dashboard. Metric `validation.rejects` up 2.5x for the past 15m. A lot of events arrive without `route_id`, so the billing system assigns them to the default/degen route.

emma (eng-platform): example offending payload we captured: `['success', {'text': 'ok'}]` vs expected `{"status": "success", "payload": {"text":"ok"}}`. Our strict-union parsing fails on the array branch.

rafael (eng-runtime): that's from legacy adapters that prefer compact tuples. Our parser currently returns reject for non-object top-level shapes. We can add a coercion layer in the runtime that normalizes common tuples to canonical object shape.

oliver (product): main risks to list: 1) silently accepting malformed outputs could mask downstream bugs, 2) customers might be billed incorrectly, 3) Console noise + NPS hit. We need a safe short-term toleration and a longer-term fix.

emma (eng-platform): short-term mitigation idea: accept the tuple->object with `coercion_applied=true` and attach `coercion_reason=tuple_to_object_adapter` and `original_route_id` to the validation event. Observability can then attribute tokens back to the original route.

priya (observability): we can propagate `original_route_id` but current ingestion strips unknown attributes for billing. I'll add a mapping so billing copy preserves `original_route_id` if present. Also adding a tag `validation.coercion_reason`.

rafael (eng-runtime): implementation caveats: validator runs after routing. If runtime normalizes and continues, we must ensure the same route_id stays attached in later stages (e.g., dequeued adapter workers). I'll add a persistent `ctx.route_id` header.

emma (eng-platform): plus a per-route validation policy: `validation.policy = {strict, tolerate, disabled}`. Payment/legal-heavy routes default to `strict`. Others can be `tolerate` during canary.

oliver (product): Console ask: show "validation breadcrumb" per-route (counts, sample examples, last seen coercion). Make the samples downloadable (redacted). Customers should be able to opt out of tolerate for their routes.

priya (observability): dashboard plan: add `validation.coercion.count` with dims `{route_id, coercion_reason, canary_bucket}`; retention 30d. Samples: 0.5% capture of offending requests stored to S3 with redaction.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: feature/validation-tolerate canary -> staging. CI green.

rafael (eng-runtime): proposed rollout: enable `tolerate` on 1% trial bucket for 24h. If stable, expand to 10% in 48h. If `coercion.count[5m] > 200 || degen_billing_delta > 7%` then automatic rollback.

emma (eng-platform): also create a safety metric that excludes soft-tolerated tokens from degen billing summaries: `billing.tokens.excluded_for_soft_validation`. Observability, can you implement?

priya (observability): yes. We'll emit `billing.attribution_override(route_id=orig)` when `original_route_id` exists on validation event. That will keep accounting intact.

oliver (product): legal check: ensure stored samples are PII-free. We'll add a redaction pipeline that strips email/SSNs before S3.

rafael (eng-runtime): adding runtime lint in adapters to warn on tuple-shape outputs. That way adapter teams can fix sources and we reduce relying on tolerant mode.

emma (eng-platform): follow-ups:
- rafael: runtime coercion + ctx.route_id persistence behind `validation.tolerate_flag`
- priya: mapping for original_route_id + new metrics + dashboard tile
- oliver: console UI copy, opt-out flow, and sample download UX
- emma: rollout doc + kill-switch runbook

priya (observability): I'll also add an audit event in the console: clicking a sample shows the raw original + coerced forms and a one-line reason.

oliver (product): timeline?

emma (eng-platform): 24h for canary soft-tolerate in staging -> prod 1% slice. 3 business days for Console tile and opt-out. 2 weeks for adapter lint rollouts and follow-up deprecations.

priya (observability): I'll create the PR for the billing-preserve mapping and the dashboard panel today.

rafael (eng-runtime): starting the feature branch now. Putting strong logging around coerced cases so Support can triage.

emma (eng-platform): thanks all. If you see other shape variants (string-only, number instead of object), drop examples here. We'll treat each coercion class separately to avoid unexpected acceptance of outright malformed payloads. :thumbsup:
